html:
The Golden Pavilion, a Zen temple in northern Kyoto, Japan. Its official name is Rokuon-ji.

It began in 1397 as the retirement villa of the shogun Ashikaga Yoshimitsu, the most powerful man in Japan, who had ended the split between rival imperial courts and opened trade with Ming China. After his death in 1408 it became a temple of Rinzai Zen, as he had wished.

The pavilion stands at the edge of a pond. Each of its three storeys is built in a different style, and the upper two are covered in gold leaf, so the building shines in the water below. It is a model of the Kitayama culture of Yoshimitsu's court, which also gave rise to noh.

In 1950 a young monk burned the pavilion down. The writer Yukio Mishima based his novel The Temple of the Golden Pavilion on the case. The building was rebuilt in 1955.
sum: The Golden Pavilion, a Zen temple in northern Kyoto, Japan. Its official name is Rokuon-ji.
